Text

Heat waves are becoming longer and more intense in many cities. Older adults, young children and people who work outdoors are at greater risk of heat-related illness. Symptoms such as dizziness, headache and confusion should not be ignored, because heatstroke can be fatal if it is not treated quickly. Health officials advise people to drink water regularly, avoid strenuous activity during the hottest hours and check on vulnerable neighbors.

Text

Firefighters have responded to more calls this year than ever before. Last night, a crew rescued a family from a burning house. Experts say that residents should install smoke alarms and must never leave candles unattended. If the alarm had worked, the family would have left the house sooner. Next month, the department will offer free training.
